article.content: Lando Norris: ‘People are not giving him enough credit’ 20-year-old sealed F1 title after finishing third in Mexico Formula One’s leading drivers have been unstinting in their praise for the new champion, Kimi Antonelli, after the Italian driver took his debut title with third place at the Mexican Grand Prix. Antonelli became the youngest world champion at 20 years old in Mexico, sharing a podium with race winner Max Verstappen and second-placed Lewis Hamilton. He has taken the title in only his second year in the sport after a remarkable season including nine wins. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Formula One’s grid has put aside fierce on-track rivalries to heap praise on **Kimi Antonelli**, with fellow drivers acknowledging the extraordinary achievement of the sport's newest titleholder. Following a dramatic weekend in North America where the Italian driver secured the championship crown, veteran competitors stepped forward to highlight the magnitude of his campaign. According to **Sport | The Guardian**, the young driver's peers emphasized that his historic success under intense pressure has earned him a place at the very top of motorsport.

## Rivals Highlight Underappreciated Pressure

According to the report from **Sport | The Guardian**, **Lando Norris** was among the most vocal supporters, arguing that public observers have failed to fully appreciate the difficulty of the Italian's maiden title run. **Norris** asserted that critics are not giving the youngster enough credit for what he has accomplished during the grueling 24-race season. The report states that **Max Verstappen** joined in the acclaim, describing the newly crowned champion’s efforts as an insane job given the immense expectations placed upon him from a very young age. 

Formula One features drivers from a wide variety of national backgrounds competing across global circuits, and achieving success in the pinnacle of motorsport requires navigating both intense media scrutiny and relentless aerodynamic and mechanical development cycles. As detailed in our previous reporting on [Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/kimi-antonelli-becomes-youngest-f-champion-with-third-place-in-mexican-gp), securing the title at just **20 years old** places him at the very head of the sport's historical record books. Further context on his milestone achievement can be found in our profile on how [Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/antonelli-heads-list-of-f-s-youngest-champions).

## Why This Matters

This universal respect from established frontrunners signals a notable shift in the paddock hierarchy, establishing the young driver as a definitive benchmark for the current generation of racers. When elite competitors publicly validate a rival's championship campaign, it deflects lingering external skepticism and cements the athlete's psychological standing within the elite tier of the sport. For global fans and commercial stakeholders, the emergence of a multi-generational title race revitalizes audience engagement and sets up high-stakes tactical battles for upcoming seasons.

## What to Watch

Observers will be tracking how team dynamics evolve during the winter development cycle, particularly how established operations adjust their car philosophies to counter the newly crowned champion. Analysts will also monitor whether rival factories accelerate upgrades early in the next calendar year to neutralize the psychological advantage gained by this breakthrough victory.

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/01/kimi-antonelli-world-champion-mexican-grand-prix-lando-norris-lewis-hamilton-max-verstappen)
